title: Efficient Approximate Logic Synthesis with Dual-Phase Iterative Framework
problem: Accelerating approximate logic synthesis for error-tolerant applications while maintaining circuit quality. ALS runtime grows rapidly as circuit size increases, offsetting energy efficiency benefits of approximation.
motivation: Approximate computing improves energy efficiency for error-tolerant workloads but synthesis automation remains bottleneck; automation must scale with circuit complexity.
method: Dual-phase iterative framework: Phase 1 performs comprehensive circuit analysis including error characterization. Phase 2 employs minimal incremental computation leveraging Phase 1 information.
key_novelty: Separating comprehensive analysis from incremental computation enables rapid re-optimization with minimal computational overhead.
contributions: 21.8x acceleration vs state-of-the-art without quality loss
Dual-phase framework reducing incremental computation per iteration
Scalable synthesis for large approximate circuits
limitations: Specific application domains and error constraints not discussed; generalization scope unclear.
